advances: Stationarity of the raw-moment ellipsoid program, for source caps with balanced base and common mass. The caps need not be depth-attaining through the selected centroid.
author: PK-research-agent
proof:
Use the compact graph and strict interpolation of the raw-moment support and interpolation lemma on the original measure. Since $t_0$ is interior, interpolation between the sections at $0$ and $T_j$ gives $J(Q_{t_0}(j))>0$. Transform the moment coordinate to $q'=A^{-1}(q-c)$ and call the transformed compact convex joint body $\mathcal B$. Its section at $t_0$ contains $B_d$. There is $\eta>0$ with $(t_0-\eta,0),(t_0+\eta,0)\in\mathcal B$. Indeed, mix the ball section with a feasible point from a mass on either side. For small mixture weight $\theta$ the new section contains a ball of radius $1-\theta$ with center of norm $O(\theta)$, hence contains zero.

A unit full normal $(r,w)\in\mathbb R\times\mathbb R^d$ is active on $\{t_0\}\times B_d$ if $h_{\mathcal B}(r,w)=r t_0+\|w\|$. The active set is closed in the unit sphere. The two neighboring feasible centers rule out $w=0$ there. With $v=w/\|w\|$ and $b=-r/\|w\|$ an active plane is $v\cdot q'\le1+b(t-t_0)$. Testing the neighboring centers gives $|b|\le1/\eta$. Hence the set of triples $(-b,v,vv^{\mathsf T})$ is compact. Its conic hull is closed: the last component of each triple has trace one, so the sum of coefficients in any convergent sequence of conic combinations stays bounded, and the convex hull of the compact triple set is compact in finite dimensions. If the active set is empty, use the closed cone $\{0\}$.

If $(0,0,I_d)$ is outside this cone, separate it from the cone to obtain a real $s$, a vector $p$ and a symmetric matrix $B$ with $\operatorname{tr}B>0$ and $-bs+v\cdot p+v^{\mathsf T}Bv\le0$ at every active triple. Replace $B$ by $B-\varepsilon I_d$ for sufficiently small positive $\varepsilon$ so its trace remains positive. The inequalities become uniformly strict. At positive variation parameter $h$, try the ellipsoid at mass $t_0+hs$ with transformed center $hp$ and shape $I_d+hB$. Its support at full normal $(r,w)$ is
$$
r(t_0+hs)+h w\cdot p+\|(I_d+hB)w\|.
$$
For $w\ne0$ its first-order change divided by $h$ at zero is $rs+w\cdot p+w^{\mathsf T}Bw/\|w\|$. On active normals this is strictly negative after division by $\|w\|$. By compactness and the lower bound on $\|w\|$ on a neighborhood of the active set, there is a neighborhood on which the derivative is uniformly negative and the support expansion is uniform. On the compact complement the original support gap to $\mathcal B$ is uniformly positive, while the support change is uniformly $O(h)$ by the triangle inequality, even when $w=0$. This proves containment for small $h>0$ by support comparison. The varied shape is positive definite and has determinant greater than one since the derivative of $\det(I_d+hB)$ is $\operatorname{tr}B>0$ at zero. Returning by $A$ would increase the volume at a feasible mass, contradicting maximality.

The target is therefore a nonnegative conic combination of active triples, giving the three identities. At most $1+d+d(d+1)/2$ nonzero coefficients suffice: if a representation uses more, a linear dependence permits changing the coefficients along it until one vanishes while all stay nonnegative. Such a dependence has coefficients of both signs by taking the trace in its last component. Iteration proves the bound. The trace of the matrix identity gives $\sum_i\lambda_i=d$.

In the original moment coordinate each selected plane supports at $q=c+Av_i$ with direction $u_i=A^{-1}v_i$ and unchanged slope $b_i$. Apply the prescribed-slope cap-duality lemma at the same $j,t_0$ and each of these nonzero directions. It gives the stated finite caps. Their balance and raw moments yield
$$
\Psi_i=u_i\cdot(c+Av_i)-t_0 b_i=u_i\cdot c+1-t_0 b_i.
$$
The three identities give $\sum_i\lambda_i\Psi_i=d$. The average measure is dominated because its normalized weights sum to one. Each constituent has the same mass and base mean; its continuous centroid is $(c+Av_i)/t_0$. The first and second vector identities give the centroid and covariance as stated. Also $\sum_i\lambda_i L_i(z,x)=\sum_i\lambda_i a_i\cdot(z-j)$. At $z=j$ this sum vanishes, so some margin is nonnegative and some is nonpositive. Taking positive parts and using subadditivity gives the integral bound.
statement:
Let $n\ge0$, $d\ge1$, and let $P\subset\mathbb Z^n$ be finite and nonempty. For each $z\in P$ let $K_z\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a compact convex body of positive $d$-volume, and set $\mu=\sum_{z\in P}\delta_z\otimes(\mathcal L^d|_{K_z})$. Call $b=(t,v)$ feasible if $\int f\,d\mu=t$ and $\int zf\,d\mu=v$ for some measurable $0\le f\le1$. For a feasible $b$ let $Q(b)$ be the set of $\int xf\,d\mu$ over those densities. For a compact convex nonempty set $Q\subset\mathbb R^d$ write $J(Q)=\max\{(\det A)^{1/d}:c+AB_d\subset Q,\ A\succeq0\}$, with $B_d$ the closed Euclidean unit ball and $A$ symmetric.

For $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ write $Q_t(j)=Q(t,tj)$ and $T_j=\max\{t:(t,tj)\text{ is feasible}\}$.

Fix $j\in\operatorname{conv}P$ and an interior maximizing mass $0<t_0<T_j$ for $J(Q_t(j))$. Let $c+AB_d$ be a maximum-volume ellipsoid of $Q_{t_0}(j)$, with $A$ symmetric positive definite. There are $m\le 1+d+d(d+1)/2$ unit vectors $v_i$, positive weights $\lambda_i$, and real slopes $b_i$ with
$$
\sum_i\lambda_i v_i=0,\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i v_i v_i^{\mathsf T}=I_d,\qquad
\sum_i\lambda_i b_i=0 .
$$
With $u_i=A^{-1}v_i$ there are finite $a_i$ and caps $H_i=\{L_i\ge0\}$, $L_i(z,x)=u_i\cdot x+a_i\cdot(z-j)-b_i$, of mass $t_0$, base mean $j$, and raw continuous moments $c+Av_i$. Put $\Psi_i=\int(L_i)_+\,d\mu$. Then $\sum_i\lambda_i\Psi_i=d$. The dominated measure $d^{-1}\sum_i\lambda_i\mu|_{H_i}$ has mass $t_0$ and centroid $(j,c/t_0)$, and the constituent continuous centroids under weights $\lambda_i/d$ have covariance $A^2/(dt_0^2)$. On the plane $z=j$, the caps $H_i$ cover the plane and so do their opposite closed halfspaces. Also
$$
\int\left[\sum_i\lambda_i a_i\cdot(z-j)\right]_+\,d\mu\le d.
$$
title: Augmented John contacts at an interior optimizing source mass
